questions.text: Real GDP measured at chained prices of the previous year, compared to real GDP measured at constant prices of a base year:

options.a: always yields a higher growth rate estimate
options.b: eliminates the need to choose a reference base year
options.c: better captures the effect of changes in relative prices on measured economic growth
options.d: is only applicable to closed economies

questions.text: A country whose Consumer Price Index (base year 2010) is equal to 140 in 2024 and whose nominal wage has increased by 25% between 2010 and 2024 has experienced:

options.a: an increase in workers' real wages between 2010 and 2024
options.b: a decrease in workers' real wages between 2010 and 2024
options.c: we cannot determine the evolution of real wages because the provided information is not enough to determine the CPI growth rate
options.d: we cannot determine the evolution of real wages without knowing the GDP deflator

questions.text: At the equilibrium on the money market, commercial banks' demand for reserves is:

options.a: decreasing along the nominal interest rate
options.b: independent of households' preference for holding currency rather than deposits
options.c: independent of the aggregate price level
options.d: increasing along the demand for currency

questions.text: The NAIRU is the unemployment rate at which:

options.b: the unemployment rate equals the frictional unemployment rate only
options.c: inflation is necessarily equal to the central bank's inflation target
options.d: the inflation rate remains stable from one period to the next

questions.text: On the money market, a liquidity trap corresponds to a situation where:

options.a: the money demand is perfectly inelastic with respect to the interest rate, so any increase in money supply raises the interest rate
options.b: the money demand is perfectly elastic with respect to the interest rate, so any increase in money supply is absorbed by agents without reducing the interest rate
options.c: the central bank is unable to use money supply so as to raise the interest rate
options.d: the central bank is unable to increase the money supply

questions.text: In the IS-LM-PC model, a persistently positive output gap implies that:

options.a: the inflation rate decreases from one period to the next
options.b: the inflation rate remains stable, as long as the central bank keeps the nominal interest rate unchanged
options.c: the inflation rate increases from one period to the next
options.d: the price level falls progressively back to its long-run equilibrium level

questions.text: The "impossible trinity" of international macroeconomics states that a country cannot simultaneously maintain:

options.a: a fixed exchange rate, free capital mobility, and an independent monetary policy
options.b: a balanced trade account, a fixed exchange rate, and full employment
options.c: price stability, economic growth, and a fixed exchange rate
options.d: a flexible exchange rate, free capital mobility, and an independent monetary policy

questions.text: In an open economy, a current account surplus implies that:

options.a: the funding capacity of the country is negative
options.b: liabilities exceed assets in the financial accounts
options.c: the trade balance is necessarily in surplus

questions.text: Compared to a closed economy, the fiscal multiplier in an open economy is smaller because:

options.a: part of the increase in domestic demand is satisfied by additional imports
options.b: the central bank systematically raises interest rates in response to fiscal expansions in open economies
options.c: a fiscal expansion necessarily leads to a currency appreciation that fully offsets the increase in government spending
options.d: households save a larger fraction of their income in open economies than in closed economies

questions.text: In the Mundell-Fleming model with a flexible exchange rate regime, an expansive fiscal policy leads to:

options.a: an increase in economic activity and a depreciation of the domestic currency
options.b: a "crowding out" of net exports via an appreciation of the domestic currency, leaving output unchanged
options.c: an increase in both the interest rate and economic activity
options.d: a depreciation of the domestic currency and an increase in net exports

questions.text: In the Solow model, two countries A and B share the same structural characteristics but start from different initial capital-to-labor ratios, with k0A > k0B. According to the standard Solow model:

options.a: Country A will grow faster than country B since it has more capital to work with
options.b: Country B will grow faster than country A since it displays higher marginal returns to capital
options.c: Both countries will grow at the same rate throughout their transition path since they share similar structural characteristics
options.d: Country A will converge to a higher steady-state capital-to-labor ratio than country B

questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer) In the Solow model:

options.a: A higher saving rate leads to a higher steady-state income per capita
options.b: A higher population growth rate leads to a lower steady-state income per capita
options.c: A higher depreciation rate leads to a lower steady-state income per capita
options.d: Two countries with the same initial capital-to-labor ratio but different saving rates will necessarily converge to the same steady-state level of income per capita
